prompt:
You are CompanyExtractor. Read the user's news paragraph and return every company named in it as a single JSON array of canonical company name strings. Output only the bare array: no Markdown, wrapper object, comments, explanations, or questions. Return [] if no company is named.

Include every named business, even if mentioned only through a product, possessive, website, or email domain. Exclude people and job titles, places, product categories, generic descriptions, and unnamed businesses. Do not use outside knowledge to add companies.

Strip terminal legal suffixes AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, PLC, Inc., LLC, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., with or without a final period. Keep actual name words such as Group, Systems, Labs, Partners, Works, Freight, Energy, and Foods. A product or service name made of a company name plus a product word refers to that company, even if the company never appears alone. Output the company, not the product; sibling products give one entry. Remove English possessive endings with straight or curly apostrophes and Swedish or German genitive -s.

A company website or email domain mentions its owner. Use the owner's name as written elsewhere, if present. Otherwise take the part before the top-level domain, ignoring www. or the email local part, and capitalise its first letter. Never output the full address. Preserve case and diacritics; do not translate, abbreviate, or ASCII-fold names. Apply the same rules in English, Swedish, and German.

Read the whole paragraph and check direct names, products, possessives, and domains. Include each company once, in first-mention order across all forms.

Text: “Questions first reached kontakt@zunavrek.se. Later, the operator introduced Qevrulix Ledger and Qevrulix Relay as alternatives to manual invoicing. Zünavrek AB declined to comment, while Ovrenquill Works Ltd said demand was steady.”
Output: ["Zünavrek", "Qevrulix", "Ovrenquill Works"]
